thread.disposition: No required code change for the covered authorization-order regression; optional broader malformed-number coverage
thread.observationAcknowledged: The fixture serializer indeed does not implement the production safe-integer input validator.
reasoning: authorizationCanonical is private to the closed synthetic receipt CLI test, not a production or reusable canonical-JSON validator.

The positive authorization comes from authorizeConsumerGate(input). For the arm/arm64 ordering regression, the exact serialized envelope is accepted by the real verify-docs-consumer-gate.mjs verify-checkout subprocess and then the independent verify-docs-cohort-v2-receipt.mjs subprocess. Both must exit successfully, so helper serialization cannot conceal production rejection of the covered positive fixture.

The real authorizer reader recomputes its digest using canonicalJson, whose number branch requires Number.isSafeInteger. The receipt reader independently recomputes authorizationDigest through its own canonicalAuthorization with the same safe-integer guard.

Every alternate authorization passed to writeAuthorization in this test is enumerated: cohort_generation becomes integer 2 with recomputed record digest; packages is deleted; asset package changes to a string. No alternate write introduces a fractional or non-finite number.

The key-order negative writes the former locale digest consistently into authorization and install evidence and asserts that the actual receipt CLI rejects it. It cannot pass solely because a fixture helper returned a digest.

The test does not claim arbitrary malformed-number canonicalizer conformance. Duplicating safe-integer checks in a fixture builder would validate fixture construction, not independently prove the production rejection boundary. A future malformed-input regression should exercise a real reader with malformed evidence.

thread.proposedReply: Reviewed against be1c81ec749aa62ddf524424ccd19284c5043a0e. The helper is a fixture serializer for this closed receipt regression; it is not the production canonical-JSON validator. The policy-3.1 fixture is produced by authorizeConsumerGate and its exact envelope must pass the real verify-checkout subprocess, followed by the separate real receipt CLI. Both readers recompute the authorization digest with the production safe-integer guard. The alternate authorization writes in this case only change an integer generation, remove packages, or change a package-name string. The locale-order negative is also submitted to the real receipt CLI and must be rejected. Therefore the missing guard in the fixture helper does not mask production rejection on any covered success path. This test does not claim malformed-number conformance; copying that guard into the builder would not establish it. No code change is required for this ordering fix.
